bougie:Le Méridien Lav (Podstrana).name: Le Méridien Lav (Podstrana)
bougie:Le Méridien Lav (Podstrana).hook: Podstrana (15 min from Split) · 5★ seaside resort — the address for luxury 15 min from the palace
bougie:Le Méridien Lav (Podstrana).text: Podstrana (15 min from Split) · 5★ seaside resort — the address for luxury 15 min from the palace Resort · seasonal rooms Essential 5★ Marriott resort on the south coast of Split, private beach, marina, several restaurants including the gastronomic Spalatum. Contemporary luxury outside the palace — comfort, not historical charm.

bougie:Vestibul Palace.name: Vestibul Palace
bougie:Vestibul Palace.hook: Diocletian's Palace · 5★ boutique hotel — rooms inside the Roman palace walls
bougie:Vestibul Palace.text: Diocletian's Palace · 5★ boutique hotel — rooms inside the Roman palace walls Months ahead in season Hotel · seasonal Boutique hotel installed in a wing of Diocletian's Palace (4th century), rooms with Roman-stone walls, peristyle view. Spectacular breakfast in a vaulted room. House restaurant, reasonable. The only way to sleep inside the palace itself.

bougie:Brač / Hvar — villas et boutique-.name: Brač / Hvar — villas et boutique-hôtels
bougie:Brač / Hvar — villas et boutique-.hook: Dalmatian islands · ferry from Split — the real luxury destination is on the islands, not in Split
bougie:Brač / Hvar — villas et boutique-.text: Dalmatian islands · ferry from Split — the real luxury destination is on the islands, not in Split Serious Dalmatian-coast luxury lives on the islands. Brač (40-min ferry): Bol and the Zlatni Rat beach, Konoba Tomić and Stina Winery (Bol). Hvar (1h30 ferry): Hvar town (boutique hotels, Michelin-Plate restaurants — Gariful, Macondo), Pakleni archipelago for private boats. Vis (2h30 ferry): the most preserved, Komiža and Vis town, indigenous wines (Vugava, Plavac Mali). Typical yacht-charter logic: Split = base, islands = destination.

dish:🍖 Pašticada à la dalmate.name: 🍖 Pašticada à la dalmate
dish:🍖 Pašticada à la dalmate.hook: Beef marinated 24h · Prošek · prunes, pork lard, rosemary — the Dalmatian Sunday dish
dish:🍖 Pašticada à la dalmate.text: Beef marinated 24h · Prošek · prunes, pork lard, rosemary — the Dalmatian Sunday dish A slice of top round of beef larded with pork fat, garlic and cloves, marinated 24 hours in wine vinegar with carrots, onions, rosemary. Braised 4 hours with dried prunes, Prošek wine (Dalmatian straw wine), tomato, sometimes Plavac Mali. Thick brown-leather sauce. Served with njoki (Croatian gnocchi, denser than Italian) that soak up the sauce. A feast dish — Sundays, weddings. Reference at Apetit et Fife .

dish:🍲 Brodet (brujet, brodetto).name: 🍲 Brodet (brujet, brodetto)
dish:🍲 Brodet (brujet, brodetto).hook: Dalmatian fish stew · tomato, white wine · polenta — cousin of bourride and caciucco
dish:🍲 Brodet (brujet, brodetto).text: Dalmatian fish stew · tomato, white wine · polenta — cousin of bourride and caciucco Several fish (red mullet, grouper, monkfish, scorpionfish, sometimes cuttlefish or langoustine), onion, garlic, crushed tomato, parsley, Dalmatian white wine, Brač or Hvar olive oil, vinegar. 30 min uncovered to reduce. Served on white polenta (palenta) or on a slice of stale bread. Direct cousin of Provençal bourride and Italian Adriatic brodetto. At Dvor , at Konoba Marjan .

dish:🦊 Peka — agneau / poulpe / veau sou.name: 🦊 Peka — agneau / poulpe / veau sous la cloche
dish:🦊 Peka — agneau / poulpe / veau sou.hook: Heated iron bell · red ashes · 2h — book 24 hours ahead
dish:🦊 Peka — agneau / poulpe / veau sou.text: Heated iron bell · red ashes · 2h — book 24 hours ahead See the funfact above. Three canonical versions: janjetina ispod peke (Dalmatian milk-lamb, usually from Brač or Pag), hobotnica ispod peke (octopus), teletina ispod peke (veal). Potatoes, carrots, onions, rosemary, sometimes olive oil. The bell traps the vapors — the meat bathes in its own juices while caramelizing at the base. 24-hour booking required everywhere. At Matejuška (octopus peka), at Šperun (lamb peka, by booking), at Dvor (milk-lamb peka).

dish:🍲 Crni rižot — squid-ink risotto.name: 🍲 Crni rižot — squid-ink risotto
dish:🍲 Crni rižot — squid-ink risotto.hook: Black rice · cuttlefish · Dalmatian white wine — cousin of Venetian black risotto
dish:🍲 Crni rižot — squid-ink risotto.text: Black rice · cuttlefish · Dalmatian white wine — cousin of Venetian black risotto The cuttlefish is cooked with its own ink, which dyes the rice deep black. Arborio or Carnaroli rice, onion, garlic, white wine (Pošip or Maraština), finished with olive oil. All'onda texture like Venice — wet, not dry. Standard along the Dalmatian coast; in Split, one of the best versions is at Konoba Fetivi .

dish:🍳 Soparnik.name: 🍳 Soparnik
dish:🍳 Soparnik.hook: Thin dough wrapper · chard, onion, olive oil — Poljica specialty, Croatian PGI since 2016
dish:🍳 Soparnik.text: Thin dough wrapper · chard, onion, olive oil — Poljica specialty, Croatian PGI since 2016 Traditional dish of Poljica, 30 km south of Split. Two paper-thin dough sheets (flour, water, salt, oil), filling of chopped chard, spring onion, garlic, parsley, plenty of Dalmatian olive oil. Traditionally baked under the ashes of an open hearth. Croatian PGI (Specijalitet zaštićenog zemljopisnog podrijetla) since 2016. Medieval fasting dish — no meat, no cheese. Ask for it in the inland konobas.

dish:🍮 Rožata.name: 🍮 Rožata
dish:🍮 Rožata.hook: Crème caramel scented with rožalin — the Dalmatian crème caramel
dish:🍮 Rožata.text: Crème caramel scented with rožalin — the Dalmatian crème caramel Traditional crème caramel from Dubrovnik and southern Dalmatia, scented with rožalin (rose-petal liqueur, once made in convents). Denser than French crème caramel, slightly curdled. Served cold. The best is in Dubrovnik (Konoba Lokanda Peskarija); several Split houses offer it.

dish:🍲 Viška pogača.name: 🍲 Viška pogača
dish:🍲 Viška pogača.hook: Vis island · anchovy, onion, tomato flatbread — the Adriatic's Venetian-style «pizza»
dish:🍲 Viška pogača.text: Vis island · anchovy, onion, tomato flatbread — the Adriatic's Venetian-style «pizza» Thin leavened dough, topped with melted onions, salted anchovies, tomatoes, sometimes capers, olive oil. Distant cousin of Naples pizza, but from a separate Adriatic tradition — pogača names a family of flatbreads across the Balkans. Vis-island specialty (sold hot from Komiža's oven). A few Split bakeries offer it on weekends — ask.

dish:🥩 Pršut + Paški sir.name: 🥩 Pršut + Paški sir
dish:🥩 Pršut + Paški sir.hook: Smoked Dalmatian ham + Pag sheep cheese — the standard apéritif platter
dish:🥩 Pršut + Paški sir.text: Smoked Dalmatian ham + Pag sheep cheese — the standard apéritif platter Pršut — pork ham dried 12 to 18 months, exposed to the bura (cold, dry northeast wind), lightly smoked in certain terroirs (Drniš, Istria). Dry texture, salinity, fragrant fat. Direct cousin of jambon de Bayonne and Tyrol Speck. Paški sir — Pag-island sheep cheese, Croatian AOP. The sheep graze on grass constantly salted by the bura , giving the milk a unique mineral signature. Hard-pressed cheese, dark rind, six months minimum aging. The best are at 36 months, dry and caramelized.

drink:🍷 Plavac Mali — le grand rouge dal.name: 🍷 Plavac Mali — le grand rouge dalmate
drink:🍷 Plavac Mali — le grand rouge dal.hook: Pelješac · Dingač, Postup · descendant of Tribidrag — structured tannins, black cherry, garrigue
drink:🍷 Plavac Mali — le grand rouge dal.text: Pelješac · Dingač, Postup · descendant of Tribidrag — structured tannins, black cherry, garrigue Dalmatia's major red variety, a crossing descended from Tribidrag (Zinfandel) and Dobričić. Grown on steep slopes of the Pelješac peninsula (southern Dalmatia) — the two grand crus are Dingač (south-facing near-terraced vines, limestone, sea wind) and Postup (north-facing). Marked tannin, 14°+ alcohol, ripe black cherry, garrigue, sometimes animal. Producers: Grgić Vina (Mike Grgich, the Croat of Napa Valley who won the Judgement of Paris 1976, returned to make wine in Dalmatia), Saints Hills, Korta Katarina. Producers Grgić Vina · Saints Hills · Korta Katarina · Bura

drink:🍷 Pošip — le grand blanc de Korčul.name: 🍷 Pošip — le grand blanc de Korčula
drink:🍷 Pošip — le grand blanc de Korčul.hook: Korčula (island) · salinity, honey, apricot — Dalmatia's near-Burgundy
drink:🍷 Pošip — le grand blanc de Korčul.text: Korčula (island) · salinity, honey, apricot — Dalmatia's near-Burgundy Indigenous white grape from Korčula island, mostly grown at Smokvica and Čara in the island's center. Atlantic salinity despite the Adriatic, apricot, honey, sometimes wild fennel. Tank-fermented for fresh styles, barrel for top cuvées. Producers: Toreta, Bire, Krajančić, PZ Pošip Čara (cooperative). Open with seafood, brodet, soparnik. Producers Toreta · Bire · Krajančić

drink:🍷 Tribidrag (Crljenak Kaštelanski.name: 🍷 Tribidrag (Crljenak Kaštelanski / Zinfandel)
drink:🍷 Tribidrag (Crljenak Kaštelanski.hook: Kaštela · ancestral grape — the original Zinfandel rootstock
drink:🍷 Tribidrag (Crljenak Kaštelanski.text: Kaštela · ancestral grape — the original Zinfandel rootstock See the funfact. In the 1990s only 9 known vines remained in Dalmatia. Today, several producers are rebuilding the vineyards — Putalj (Kaštel Sućurac, 15 km from Split), Mihovil, Brkić. Generally more fluid in style than Plavac Mali, closer to Italian Primitivo than to California Zinfandel. Worth tasting for the historical curiosity as much as for the wine.

drink:🍷 Vugava — indigenous Vis grape va.name: 🍷 Vugava — indigenous Vis grape variety
drink:🍷 Vugava — indigenous Vis grape va.hook: Vis island · small production — rare grape, perfectly suited to the island climate
drink:🍷 Vugava — indigenous Vis grape va.text: Vis island · small production — rare grape, perfectly suited to the island climate Indigenous white grape almost exclusive to Vis island (the most remote in Dalmatia). Gives structured, saline, slightly fat whites that age well. Very limited production. Reference: Lipanović, Roki's, PZ Vis (cooperative). A bottle to take home for lovers of niche whites.

drink:🍇 Prošek — vin de paille dalmate.name: 🍇 Prošek — vin de paille dalmate
drink:🍇 Prošek — vin de paille dalmate.hook: Straw-dried grapes · sweet · residual sugar — served with rožata or as apéritif
drink:🍇 Prošek — vin de paille dalmate.text: Straw-dried grapes · sweet · residual sugar — served with rožata or as apéritif Dalmatian sweet wine made from grapes dried on racks (passito method). Cousin of the Jura's Vin de Paille, Friuli's Picolit, Venice's Recioto. Varieties: Plavac Mali for red, Maraština or Bogdanuša for white. High residual sugar, 14° alcohol. Served as apéritif, at meal's end, or used in cooking for pašticada. The legal dispute with Italy over the «Prosek/Prosecco» name is ongoing — don't confuse them.

drink:🌲 Rakija — eau-de-vie de fruit ou.name: 🌲 Rakija — eau-de-vie de fruit ou d'herbes
drink:🌲 Rakija — eau-de-vie de fruit ou.hook: Šljivovica, travarica, kruškovac · 40° — apéritif and digestif — whatever the house has on hand
drink:🌲 Rakija — eau-de-vie de fruit ou.text: Šljivovica, travarica, kruškovac · 40° — apéritif and digestif — whatever the house has on hand Balkan family of eaux-de-vie. Šljivovica — plum, the standard; travarica — herb maceration (sage, rosemary, thyme, wild fennel, up to 30 plants), Dalmatian specialty; kruškovac — pear; orahovac — green walnuts; medenica — honey. Served everywhere, at all hours, on every occasion. The Dalmatian peasant version sold by the maker holds its own. Decent industrial brand: Maraska (since 1899, Zadar). Buy direct from the producer or at the market.

drink:Paradox Wine & Cheese Bar.name: Paradox Wine & Cheese Bar
drink:Paradox Wine & Cheese Bar.hook: Centre · €6–12 a glass — the Croatian-wine reference in Split · sommelier who explains plainly
drink:Paradox Wine & Cheese Bar.text: Centre · €6–12 a glass — the Croatian-wine reference in Split · sommelier who explains plainly See the entry . Wide Croatian wine list, from Pelješac (Plavac Mali) cellars to Plešivica (continental, sparkling, Pinot Gris). Cheese boards (Paški sir, Skuta, Tilan). Sommelier who explains plainly. Open late. The after-dinner stop.

drink:☕ D16 Coffee — troisième vague.name: ☕ D16 Coffee — troisième vague
drink:☕ D16 Coffee — troisième vague.hook: Palace · €2–5 espresso — one of the only serious specialty coffees on the Dalmatian coast
drink:☕ D16 Coffee — troisième vague.text: Palace · €2–5 espresso — one of the only serious specialty coffees on the Dalmatian coast See the entry . A third-wave pioneer in Split, serious roastery. Small shop in a palace alley. V60, espresso, flat white. Croatian or Ethiopian beans. The serious morning caffeine stop.

music:🎵 Splitsko ljeto / Split Summer Fe.name: 🎵 Splitsko ljeto / Split Summer Festival
music:🎵 Splitsko ljeto / Split Summer Fe.hook: Mid-July to mid-August · peristyle, palace — opera and theatre in the Roman palace since 1954
music:🎵 Splitsko ljeto / Split Summer Fe.text: Mid-July to mid-August · peristyle, palace — opera and theatre in the Roman palace since 1954 Split's summer festival, founded 1954. Opera, theater, classical music, ballet programming. Diocletian's palace peristyle serves as an open-air stage; the acoustics of the Roman walls do the rest. Aida, Carmen, Tosca have been performed in the ancient setting. Program announced every spring. When Mid-July to mid-August

music:🎬 Mediterranean Film Festival Spli.name: 🎬 Mediterranean Film Festival Split
music:🎬 Mediterranean Film Festival Spli.hook: Summer · Mediterranean cinema — Adriatic-coast film festival
music:🎬 Mediterranean Film Festival Spli.text: Summer · Mediterranean cinema — Adriatic-coast film festival International Mediterranean film festival held every summer in Split. Programming of Croatian films and films from the southern shore (Italy, Greece, Spain, Maghreb). Verify the 2026 dates.

music:🎼 Klapa — chant polyphonique dalma.name: 🎼 Klapa — chant polyphonique dalmate (UNESCO)
music:🎼 Klapa — chant polyphonique dalma.hook: Summer festivals · palace concerts — UNESCO Intangible Heritage 2012
music:🎼 Klapa — chant polyphonique dalma.text: Summer festivals · palace concerts — UNESCO Intangible Heritage 2012 Klapa is a Dalmatian a-cappella polyphonic song, six to ten male voices (sometimes female), maritime, love, religious themes. A village tradition transposed to concert since the 19th century. UNESCO Intangible Heritage since 2012. The central festival is the Festival Dalmatinskih Klapa Omiš , in Omiš (25 km from Split, June–July). In Split, several informal peristyle concerts in summer — free, tourist-friendly but authentic.

music:🎷 Parasol — listening bar audiophi.name: 🎷 Parasol — listening bar audiophile
music:🎷 Parasol — listening bar audiophi.hook: Palace (Adamova 5) · New Fidelity system · vinyl — the only one on the Dalmatian coast
music:🎷 Parasol — listening bar audiophi.text: Palace (Adamova 5) · New Fidelity system · vinyl — the only one on the Dalmatian coast See the entry . Listening bar in the Japanese jazz-kissa lineage (bars where you listen to music on a custom hi-fi system without talking too loud). Bespoke New Fidelity (Frankfurt) system in-room. Vinyl, ASC (Animal Society Club, Split label) resident DJs at weekends. Go early — before 9pm to hear the room before it fills.

culture:Palais de Dioclétien.name: Palais de Dioclétien
culture:Palais de Dioclétien.hook: UNESCO 1979 · free — 215 × 180 m rectangular plan, 4th c.
culture:Palais de Dioclétien.text: UNESCO 1979 · free — 215 × 180 m rectangular plan, 4th c. Free (access) · €4–6 for cathedral, substructures, baptistery See the funfact. Four original gates: Golden Gate (north), Silver Gate (east), Bronze Gate (south, sea-facing), Iron Gate (west). The peristyle (colonnaded court) at the heart. The substructures are almost entirely preserved — Game of Thrones episodes 8–10 were filmed here. Cathedral (Diocletian's former octagonal mausoleum, ironically reconverted to a Christian church in the 7th century), Temple of Jupiter (now the baptistery). What to see Peristyle · substructures · cathedral · baptistery

culture:Cathédrale Saint-Domnius.name: Cathédrale Saint-Domnius
culture:Cathédrale Saint-Domnius.text: Palace · €4–6 — Diocletian's former mausoleum, 4th c. Octagonal mausoleum built by Diocletian (himself a persecutor of Christians) to house his own tomb. In the 7th century reconverted into a Christian cathedral and named after Saint Domnius (Sveti Duje), bishop martyr of Salona, killed in the Diocletianic persecution — perfect historical irony. 13th-c. Romanesque bell tower (60 m, paid climb, panorama over palace and bay). Carved-wood doors by Andrija Buvina (1214). Treasury. What to see Mausoleum · bell tower · Buvina doors

culture:Galerija Meštrović.name: Galerija Meštrović
culture:Galerija Meštrović.hook: Foot of Marjan (15-min walk from centre) · €8–10 — house-studio of Ivan Meštrović, Croatia's 20th-c. sculptor
culture:Galerija Meštrović.text: Foot of Marjan (15-min walk from centre) · €8–10 — house-studio of Ivan Meštrović, Croatia's 20th-c. sculptor 8–10 € Ivan Meštrović (1883–1962), the great 20th-century Croatian sculptor, a Rodin student, built this villa in Split in 1939 as a house-studio. Today a museum. Monumental sculptures (Mother and Son, Cycle of Job), bas-reliefs, drawings. Combine with Kaštelet-Crikvine Meštrović 200 m away (a chapel decorated with a wood-bas-relief cycle). What to see House-studio · monumental sculptures · chapel

culture:Musée archéologique de Split.name: Musée archéologique de Split
culture:Musée archéologique de Split.hook: North centre · €4–6 — oldest museum in Croatia (1820)
culture:Musée archéologique de Split.text: North centre · €4–6 — oldest museum in Croatia (1820) The oldest museum in Croatia, founded 1820. Roman collection (mosaics, statues, sarcophagi, artefacts from Salona, the former Roman capital of Dalmatia 5 km north of Split), Greek (Issa, the ancient Greek colony on Vis), Illyrian. The 4th-century Good Shepherd sarcophagus is one of the highlights. What to see Good Shepherd sarcophagus · Roman Salona · Greek Issa

culture:Salona — capitale romaine de la.name: Salona — capitale romaine de la Dalmatie
culture:Salona — capitale romaine de la.hook: Solin (15 min from Split) · €5–7 — amphitheater, basilica, urban remains 1st–7th c.
culture:Salona — capitale romaine de la.text: Solin (15 min from Split) · €5–7 — amphitheater, basilica, urban remains 1st–7th c. 5–7 € Ancient Salona (today Solin) was the capital of Roman Dalmatia (1st c. BC to 7th c. AD) — up to 60,000 inhabitants in the 3rd century. Destroyed by the Avars and Slavs in the 7th century, which pushed the population to take refuge in Diocletian's palace (the birth of Split). Today: amphitheater (15,000 seats), 4th-c. paleo-Christian basilica, Manastirine necropolis, theater. Vast site, allow 2h. What to see Amphitheater · basilica · Manastirine

culture:Trogir — ville-musée UNESCO.name: Trogir — ville-musée UNESCO
culture:Trogir — ville-musée UNESCO.hook: Trogir (30 min from Split) · UNESCO 1997 · free — fully-preserved medieval town
culture:Trogir — ville-musée UNESCO.text: Trogir (30 min from Split) · UNESCO 1997 · free — fully-preserved medieval town Free (access) · €5–7 individual sites Small fortified town on a small island, 30 km west of Split. UNESCO 1997. St Lawrence Cathedral (13th c., Romanesque portal by Master Radovan, one of the masterpieces of medieval Croatian art), Kamerlengo fortress, Venetian alleys, Cipiko Palace. Denser, more medieval, quieter than Split. Half a day minimum. What to see St Lawrence Cathedral · Radovan portal · Kamerlengo

culture:🌲 Marjan — parc forestier.name: 🌲 Marjan — parc forestier
culture:🌲 Marjan — parc forestier.hook: Foot of Veli Varoš · free — 178 ha · medieval hermitage chapels · panoramic trail
culture:🌲 Marjan — parc forestier.text: Foot of Veli Varoš · free — 178 ha · medieval hermitage chapels · panoramic trail Split's green lung. 178 ha of Mediterranean pinewoods (Aleppo pine, cypress, rosemary, mastic), six medieval hermit chapels (St George, St Nicholas, St Helen). Marked trail from the foot of Veli Varoš to the first terrace (15 min, view over city and palace), second terrace (45 min, Brač and Hvar views), zoo at the bottom. Bene beach to the northwest. Cycling possible. When All day · dawn and sunset for the light

work:Marjan — banc de la première terras.name: Marjan — banc de la première terrasse
work:Marjan — banc de la première terras.hook: Marked trail · free — panorama over palace + bay
work:Marjan — banc de la première terras.text: Marked trail · free — panorama over palace + bay 15-min walk from Veli Varoš. Stone, bench, Aleppo pine, plunging view over Diocletian's Palace and the bay. At dawn and sunset, golden light. The quintessential breath-pause in Split.

work:D16 Coffee.name: D16 Coffee
work:D16 Coffee.hook: Palace · Dosud 9 alley — WiFi, third-wave coffee, low-vault echo
work:D16 Coffee.text: Palace · Dosud 9 alley — WiFi, third-wave coffee, low-vault echo See the entry . Small shop in a palace alley. Tight tables, but for two hours of focused work, perfect. WiFi is fine.

work:Bajamonti — terrasse de la Prokurat.name: Bajamonti — terrasse de la Prokurative
work:Bajamonti — terrasse de la Prokurat.hook: Trg Republike (Prokurative) · chic café-resto — Habsburg neo-Renaissance café
work:Bajamonti — terrasse de la Prokurat.text: Trg Republike (Prokurative) · chic café-resto — Habsburg neo-Renaissance café See the entry . Beautiful Habsburg setting. Decent espresso in the morning. La place de la Prokurative (1859, designed by Vicko Andrić on the model of Saint Mark's Square in Venice) is one of the most beautiful squares in central Europe.

work:Riva — promenade en front de mer.name: Riva — promenade en front de mer
work:Riva — promenade en front de mer.hook: Centre, along the bay · free — café-bar every 50 m
work:Riva — promenade en front de mer.text: Centre, along the bay · free — café-bar every 50 m Split's urban promenade, 250 m facing the bay, palms, café-bars. Touristy but useful: for an hour of watching, the city's rhythm passes here. Order a Pošip by the glass anywhere, watch the ferries leave for Brač and Hvar.

work:🏔 Plage Bačvice.name: 🏔 Plage Bačvice
work:🏔 Plage Bačvice.hook: 10-min walk from centre · free — urban sand beach · Dalmatian picigin
work:🏔 Plage Bačvice.text: 10-min walk from centre · free — urban sand beach · Dalmatian picigin Sand beach (rare in Dalmatia where everything is pebbles), 10 min walk from the center. Shallow water — you can walk 30 m offshore without going over the waist. This is where picigin is played — a Dalmatian beach sport: pass a small ball by slapping the water with the palm, never letting it drop, with diving saves. Croatian intangible heritage sport. A late-afternoon show to watch.

events:✨ Sudamja — Saint-Domnius.name: ✨ Sudamja — Saint-Domnius
events:✨ Sudamja — Saint-Domnius.hook: 7 May · Split's patron-saint feast — processions, marathon, concerts
events:✨ Sudamja — Saint-Domnius.text: 7 May · Split's patron-saint feast — processions, marathon, concerts On 7 May, Split celebrates its patron saint Saint Domnius (Sveti Duje), bishop martyr of Salona who died around 304 in the Diocletianic persecutions (yes — the same emperor whose palace stands before you). Morning procession from the cathedral bell tower, urban marathon (Sudamja Run, 10 km), craft fair, open-air concerts, klapa at the peristyle. More local and more authentic than Splitsko ljeto in July. When 7 May (Sveti Duje)

events:🎵 Splitsko ljeto / Split Summer F.name: 🎵 Splitsko ljeto / Split Summer Festival
events:🎵 Splitsko ljeto / Split Summer F.hook: Mid-July to mid-August — opera, theater, ballet inside the palace · since 1954
events:🎵 Splitsko ljeto / Split Summer F.text: Mid-July to mid-August — opera, theater, ballet inside the palace · since 1954 See the Music section. Central festival of Split's cultural summer, since 1954. Aida, Carmen, Tosca at the peristyle.

events:🎬 Mediterranean Film Festival.name: 🎬 Mediterranean Film Festival
events:🎬 Mediterranean Film Festival.hook: Summer · Mediterranean cinema — verify annual edition
events:🎬 Mediterranean Film Festival.text: Summer · Mediterranean cinema — verify annual edition International Mediterranean film festival in Split — verify the date and 2026 programming.

events:🎉 Ultra Europe.name: 🎉 Ultra Europe
events:🎉 Ultra Europe.hook: Mid-July · Park Mladeži & Hvar — mainstream EDM festival · 150,000 people
events:🎉 Ultra Europe.text: Mid-July · Park Mladeži & Hvar — mainstream EDM festival · 150,000 people One of Europe's three largest electronic festivals. Three days at Park Mladeži stadium in Split, plus «Ultra Beach» on Hvar and «Resistance» on Brač island. Mainstream EDM (David Guetta, Tiësto, Hardwell). Not an underground scene — but 150,000 people in town for three days. Lodging anywhere in Dalmatia during this week is impossible without booking long ahead. When Mid-July

events:🎼 Festival des Klapa — Omiš.name: 🎼 Festival des Klapa — Omiš
events:🎼 Festival des Klapa — Omiš.hook: June–July · Omiš (25 min from Split) — the central klapa festival · since 1967
events:🎼 Festival des Klapa — Omiš.text: June–July · Omiš (25 min from Split) — the central klapa festival · since 1967 National klapa festival, held every year in Omiš (25 min south of Split, at the Cetina mouth) since 1967. This is where the best Dalmatian ensembles perform, open-air on the main square, in front of the cathedral. UNESCO Intangible Heritage since 2012. When June–July

events:✨ Procession féerique de Saint-Tr.name: ✨ Procession féerique de Saint-Tryphon — Kotor (Bouches de Kotor) — alternative
events:✨ Procession féerique de Saint-Tr.hook: 3 February · Montenegro — verify — for travelers pushing the coast further south
events:✨ Procession féerique de Saint-Tr.text: 3 February · Montenegro — verify — for travelers pushing the coast further south For reference, for travelers pushing the coast further south (Dubrovnik, Montenegro): the Saint Tryphon procession in Kotor (Montenegro) on 3 February. Outside Croatia. Verify if the Adriatic route includes Kotor.

walks:🔔 Palace at dawn.name: 🔔 Palace at dawn
walks:🔔 Palace at dawn.hook: 06:30 · Golden Gate → peristyle → substructures · 45 min — the alleys before the cruise-ships
walks:🔔 Palace at dawn.text: 06:30 · Golden Gate → peristyle → substructures · 45 min — the alleys before the cruise-ships Enter through the Golden Gate (Zlatna vrata, north) at 06:30 — outside, Meštrović's colossal Grgur Ninski statue (touching the thumb brings luck, local tradition). Descend the cardo, cross the peristyle — slanted light on the pink-granite Egyptian columns (brought from Egypt by Diocletian, from the Temple of Hatshepsut). Substructures at 09:00 when they open. Out through the Bronze Gate (south) onto the Riva, café-balcon facing the sea. When 06:30–08:00

walks:🏔 Marjan — circuit complet.name: 🏔 Marjan — circuit complet
walks:🏔 Marjan — circuit complet.hook: Veli Varoš → 1st terrace → Bene · 2h — 178 ha of pinewoods · hermitage chapels
walks:🏔 Marjan — circuit complet.text: Veli Varoš → 1st terrace → Bene · 2h — 178 ha of pinewoods · hermitage chapels From Veli Varoš (stone staircase, 25 steps), climb to Telegrin (175 m, Marjan summit) — passing the chapel of St Nicholas (13th c.), St Jerome (15th c.), St Helena. First panoramic terrace (15 min, palace view), second (45 min, Brač and Hvar view). Down the north side, Bene beach, back via the Sustipan promontory. Plenty of Aleppo pine, rosemary, mastic, with spectacular May–June blooms. Duration 2 h

walks:🚕 Trogir — demi-journée.name: 🚕 Trogir — demi-journée
walks:🚕 Trogir — demi-journée.hook: Bus 37 or car · 30 min — UNESCO medieval city on an island
walks:🚕 Trogir — demi-journée.text: Bus 37 or car · 30 min — UNESCO medieval city on an island 30 km west of Split. Fortified medieval city on a small island, connected by two bridges. UNESCO 1997. St Lawrence Cathedral (portal by Master Radovan, 1240 — Romanesque masterpiece), Kamerlengo fortress, Cipiko Palace, Venetian alleys (Trogir was under Venice 1420–1797). Half a day minimum. Lunch in a local konoba.

walks:🏯 Salona — cité romaine.name: 🏯 Salona — cité romaine
walks:🏯 Salona — cité romaine.hook: Solin (15 min) · archaeological site — 15,000-seat amphitheater, 4th-c. basilica
walks:🏯 Salona — cité romaine.text: Solin (15 min) · archaeological site — 15,000-seat amphitheater, 4th-c. basilica Ancient Salona, the Roman capital of Dalmatia, 5 km north of Split (commune of Solin). 60,000 inhabitants in the 3rd century. Remains: amphitheater (15,000 seats), 4th-c. paleo-Christian basilica, Manastirine necropolis, theater, baths. Vast site, 2h to walk. Combine with an excursion to Klis (high medieval fortress, panoramic view — Game of Thrones filming location, Meereen).

walks:🏝 Brač — demi-journée île.name: 🏝 Brač — demi-journée île
walks:🏝 Brač — demi-journée île.hook: Ferry Split → Supetar · 50 min — Bol and Zlatni Rat beach
walks:🏝 Brač — demi-journée île.text: Ferry Split → Supetar · 50 min — Bol and Zlatni Rat beach Jadrolinija ferry from Split to Supetar (north Brač port, 50 min crossing), bus to Bol (south, 1h). The Zlatni Rat beach (the "Golden Horn" — a white-pebble cape that shifts orientation with currents) is Dalmatia's postcard image. Stina wines (modern cellar carved into stone, tastings). Brač stone quarry, source of the White House in Washington. Brač pršut.

secret-gems:🌊 Bačvice · pointe est de ga.name: 🌊 Bačvice · pointe est de galets · 06:00
secret-gems:🌊 Bačvice · pointe est de ga.hook: Bačvice beach · past the last cabin — fishermen mending their nets · no tourists before 09:00
secret-gems:🌊 Bačvice · pointe est de ga.text: Bačvice beach · past the last cabin — fishermen mending their nets · no tourists before 09:00 Bačvice beach is Split's icon — fine sand, shallow water, the home ground of picigin (local game: a ball that must never touch the water). At 6am, walk past the cabins east to the pebble point: one or two fishermen mending nets in silence. The sun rises over Mosor (the massif behind), Hvar takes on a rose-ash color. Not a tourist before 9am.

secret-gems:🌉 Le péristyle · minuit en n.name: 🌉 Le péristyle · minuit en novembre
secret-gems:🌉 Le péristyle · minuit en n.hook: Heart of Diocletian's Palace · after 23:30 — cold Egyptian marbles · a 1500 BC sphinx
secret-gems:🌉 Le péristyle · minuit en n.text: Heart of Diocletian's Palace · after 23:30 — cold Egyptian marbles · a 1500 BC sphinx Diocletian's peristyle is the palace's central court (305 AD). In tourist daytime, it's a scrum. But at midnight in November, after the last waiters leave, you can sit on the Vestibule steps, beneath the Egyptian black-granite sphinx (15th c. BC, reused by Diocletian). The marble keeps the sea's cold. The acoustic resonance is made for voice: this is where the klape sing a cappella in summer.

secret-gems:🌲 Marjan · sentier sud · sor.name: 🌲 Marjan · sentier sud · sortie Sustipan
secret-gems:🌲 Marjan · sentier sud · sor.hook: Marjan · southwest path 30 min — cypresses, Aleppo pines, Brač at sunrise
secret-gems:🌲 Marjan · sentier sud · sor.text: Marjan · southwest path 30 min — cypresses, Aleppo pines, Brač at sunrise Marjan hill is Split's lung (the "Central Park of Split" locals say, but older). The south path, starting from Sustipan park (former Venetian cemetery, dismantled), runs above the sea. At 7am, the first locals walk their dogs. Stone benches every 200 m. At the end, a clean view of Brač cut against the dawn. When 06:30–08:00

secret-gems:🍷 Matejuška · evening · vin.name: 🍷 Matejuška · evening · vin au gobelet
secret-gems:🍷 Matejuška · evening · vin.hook: Small fishermen's port · west of the Riva · evening — locals gather here with a bottle from the Pazar
secret-gems:🍷 Matejuška · evening · vin.text: Small fishermen's port · west of the Riva · evening — locals gather here with a bottle from the Pazar Matejuška is Split's small fishermen's harbor — at the western end of the Riva, where the boats line up on stone. No bar, no service: you sit on the stone blocks, bring your bottle from the Pazar (direct-from-producer wine, €5/L), a piece of pršut, a Kaštela tomato. It's Split's 7pm social ritual, off season. In summer, it's younger and denser.

secret-gems:🏛 Toits du palais depuis le.name: 🏛 Toits du palais depuis le campanile de Saint-Domnius
secret-gems:🏛 Toits du palais depuis le.hook: Cathedral · Romanesque-Gothic bell tower · morning — the Roman grid still readable · Mosor in the distance
secret-gems:🏛 Toits du palais depuis le.text: Cathedral · Romanesque-Gothic bell tower · morning — the Roman grid still readable · Mosor in the distance The campanile of St Domnius (13th–16th c., rebuilt in the 19th) dominates the palace. Climb at opening (8am): you see the Roman grid of the palace, still perfectly legible 1,700 years later, and behind it the Mosor massif (1,339 m), often snow-capped in winter. €7. Steep stairs — not for claustrophobes, even less for vertigo sufferers. Empty until 9:30am. When 08:00–09:00

street-food:🤬 Burek du morning · Pekarna.name: 🤬 Burek du morning · Pekarna Bobis · Marmontova
street-food:🤬 Burek du morning · Pekarna.hook: Pekarna Bobis · opens 6am — burek meso, sirnica cheese, krumpiruša potato · fresh phyllo dough
street-food:🤬 Burek du morning · Pekarna.text: Pekarna Bobis · opens 6am — burek meso, sirnica cheese, krumpiruša potato · fresh phyllo dough ~2 € Pekarna Bobis is Split's historic bakery chain — bought 1980, several locations including a flagship on Marmontova. At 6am, you take the burek still warm: meso (minced meat + onion, the classic), sirnica (fresh sheep cheese), krumpiruša (potato + cheese), sometimes zeljanica (spinach). Hand-stretched phyllo, heavy with clarified butter. With a tart drinkable yogurt. €2. What young Croats eat coming out of clubs. Hour 06:00–14:00

street-food:🥩 Ćevapi à la grille · Kantu.name: 🥩 Ćevapi à la grille · Kantun Paulina
street-food:🥩 Ćevapi à la grille · Kantu.hook: Kantun Paulina · centre · lunch–evening — 10 ćevapi + somun + kajmak + ajvar · charcoal
street-food:🥩 Ćevapi à la grille · Kantu.text: Kantun Paulina · centre · lunch–evening — 10 ćevapi + somun + kajmak + ajvar · charcoal 5–9 € Kantun Paulina is the reference ćevabdžinica in central Split (since the 1970s). Ćevapi (small beef-lamb sausage-patties, skinless, charcoal-grilled) are served by 5 or 10, with a warm somun pocket, creamy kajmak, spicy ajvar, and raw chopped onion. It's Split's serious stand-up meal — not fast food, an institution. Hour 11:00–23:00

street-food:🍩 Fritule · Advent & winter.name: 🍩 Fritule · Advent & winter · fenêtres du marché
street-food:🍩 Fritule · Advent & winter.hook: Pazar and surroundings · Nov–Feb — small round doughnuts, raisins, rum, icing sugar
street-food:🍩 Fritule · Advent & winter.text: Pazar and surroundings · Nov–Feb — small round doughnuts, raisins, rum, icing sugar Fritule are small round Dalmatian doughnuts — rum-scented leavened dough, raisins, lemon zest, fried in hot oil, dusted with icing sugar. They appear late November in temporary windows around the Pazar and the Christmas market (Riva, December). Six for €3 in a paper cone. Eat standing, scalding hot. Gone by Easter. Season Nov–Feb

street-food:🥪 Sandwich-marinière · Bilan.name: 🥪 Sandwich-marinière · Bilan (Buffet Fife)
street-food:🥪 Sandwich-marinière · Bilan.hook: Buffet Fife · Trumbićeva obala · Matejuška — cuttlefish chiffonade, marinated anchovies, pršut, Dalmatian bread
street-food:🥪 Sandwich-marinière · Bilan.text: Buffet Fife · Trumbićeva obala · Matejuška — cuttlefish chiffonade, marinated anchovies, pršut, Dalmatian bread 5–12 € Buffet Fife (locals call it "Bilan") is a sailor's counter-kitchen on Matejuška harbor. At noon, fishermen and sailors come for a quick sandwich or a "by mood" plate: grilled cuttlefish, marinated anchovies, pršut, fish soup depending on the catch. It sits exactly between workers' canteen and fisherman's kitchen. No menu, no card — you ask what there is today. Hour Midday–3pm, evening

gastronomy:🍄 Pazar — marché vert.name: 🍄 Pazar — marché vert
gastronomy:🍄 Pazar — marché vert.hook: At the foot of the Silver Gate · 7am–2pm — fruit, vegetables, cheese, honey, pršut
gastronomy:🍄 Pazar — marché vert.text: At the foot of the Silver Gate · 7am–2pm — fruit, vegetables, cheese, honey, pršut See the entry . Historic open-air market against the palace's east wall (Silver Gate). Kaštela tomatoes, dried smokva (Brač figs), Pag sheep cheese, Marjan honey, Hvar olive oil, Drniš pršut, herbs. At 8am for the real producers — by noon it's tired.

gastronomy:🍥 Ribarnica — marché aux pois.name: 🍥 Ribarnica — marché aux poissons
gastronomy:🍥 Ribarnica — marché aux pois.hook: Marmontova · 1890 hall · morning until 1pm — neo-Renaissance, neighbouring sulfur = no flies
gastronomy:🍥 Ribarnica — marché aux pois.text: Marmontova · 1890 hall · morning until 1pm — neo-Renaissance, neighbouring sulfur = no flies See the entry . 1890 neo-Renaissance hall. Local legend: no flies in the hall because the neighboring sulfur springs (Split's thermal baths, 20 m away) emit enough sulfur to repel them. True or false, the absence of flies is observed. Morning Dalmatian fish: cuttlefish, red mullet, line sea bass, gilt-head bream. Opens early, closes around 1pm.

gastronomy:🍄 Marché de Trogir.name: 🍄 Marché de Trogir
gastronomy:🍄 Marché de Trogir.hook: Trogir (30 min) · morning — more rural, quieter
gastronomy:🍄 Marché de Trogir.text: Trogir (30 min) · morning — more rural, quieter Small morning market on Trogir's quay, more rural and quieter than Split's. Combine with the UNESCO city visit.

gastronomy:🍷 Grgić Vina — Plavac Mali.name: 🍷 Grgić Vina — Plavac Mali
gastronomy:🍷 Grgić Vina — Plavac Mali.hook: Trstenik (Pelješac, 3h from Split) · by appointment — Mike Grgich, the Croat of the Judgement of Paris 1976
gastronomy:🍷 Grgić Vina — Plavac Mali.text: Trstenik (Pelješac, 3h from Split) · by appointment — Mike Grgich, the Croat of the Judgement of Paris 1976 Mike Grgich, a Croatian vintner who emigrated to California after WWII, won the Judgement of Paris in 1976 with a Napa Valley Chardonnay (Chateau Montelena 1973) that beat the white Burgundy First Growths in blind tasting — a historic turning point for world viticulture. He returned to Croatia in 1996 and founded Grgić Vina in Trstenik (Pelješac). Plavac Mali Pelješac, Pošip Korčula. Visits by appointment. 3h from Split. Visit By appointment Address Trstenik, Pelješac

gastronomy:🍷 Stina Winery — Bol (Brač).name: 🍷 Stina Winery — Bol (Brač)
gastronomy:🍷 Stina Winery — Bol (Brač).hook: Bol (Brač, 50-min ferry) · visit and tasting — cellar carved into Brač stone
gastronomy:🍷 Stina Winery — Bol (Brač).text: Bol (Brač, 50-min ferry) · visit and tasting — cellar carved into Brač stone A modern cellar in Bol (Brač), carved into the white Brač stone (the same stone as the White House in Washington). They vinify Plavac Mali, Pošip, Vugava (rare outside Vis). Guided tours with tastings. Combine with a day on Brač and the Zlatni Rat beach. Visit Tasting shop open · guided visits by booking Address Bol, Brač

gastronomy:🧀 Paški sir — Pag.name: 🧀 Paški sir — Pag
gastronomy:🧀 Paški sir — Pag.hook: Pag island (3h from Split) · cooperative visits — PDO sheep cheese, sheep graze grass salted by the bura
gastronomy:🧀 Paški sir — Pag.text: Pag island (3h from Split) · cooperative visits — PDO sheep cheese, sheep graze grass salted by the bura The island of Pag (3h northwest of Split) is one of Europe's barest landscapes: stone, wind, sheep. The bura (northeast wind) sprays the grass with constant sea salt that the sheep ingest — uniquely mineralized milk. Paški sir (AOP) is hard-pressed, six months minimum, up to 24–36 months for the best. Visites de fromageries (Sirana Gligora, Sirana Paška) by booking. Buy at the Pazar in Split without having to go up to Pag.

gastronomy:🥕 Sel de Pag — Solana Pag.name: 🥕 Sel de Pag — Solana Pag
gastronomy:🥕 Sel de Pag — Solana Pag.hook: Pag (3h) · salt-pan visit — the Adriatic's historic salt-works · since 999
gastronomy:🥕 Sel de Pag — Solana Pag.text: Pag (3h) · salt-pan visit — the Adriatic's historic salt-works · since 999 Pag's salt pan is documented since 999 AD (one of Europe's oldest still-active salt-works). Production by solar evaporation. Table salt, hand-harvested fleur de sel between June and September. Shop on site, salt-pan tours. Pag salt has its own mineral signature — sea, sun, wind.

gastronomy:🍃 Uje Oil Bar — huiles d'oliv.name: 🍃 Uje Oil Bar — huiles d'olive croates
gastronomy:🍃 Uje Oil Bar — huiles d'oliv.hook: Centre · Marulićeva 1 · tasting €5–15 — Brač, Hvar, Istria: Croatia plays in Liguria's league
gastronomy:🍃 Uje Oil Bar — huiles d'oliv.text: Centre · Marulićeva 1 · tasting €5–15 — Brač, Hvar, Istria: Croatia plays in Liguria's league See the entry . The first shop-bar in Croatia dedicated to olive oil. Tasting flights of Brač oils (minerality, almond), Hvar (sweetness, fruit), Istrie (roundness, cut grass). Bottles to take home. Brač Bunja and Hvarska Žutica are the two PDO references. A €25 bottle travels and lands well at home. Address Marulićeva 1, Centre

avoid:⚠ Unmarked «house wine» on the per.name: ⚠ Unmarked «house wine» on the peristyle
avoid:⚠ Unmarked «house wine» on the per.hook: Peristyle terraces — poured-by-the-pitcher pours that are bulk Macedonian, not Croatian
avoid:⚠ Unmarked «house wine» on the per.text: Peristyle terraces — poured-by-the-pitcher pours that are bulk Macedonian, not Croatian Several palace bars pour an «our house wine» from anonymous pitchers — almost always bulk industrial Macedonian or low-grade Vranac, marked up to Plavac Mali prices. Ask for a labelled bottle (Plavac Mali, Pošip), or walk to Paradox or Zinfandel for the real card.

avoid:⚠ Confusing Prošek with Prosecco.name: ⚠ Confusing Prošek with Prosecco
avoid:⚠ Confusing Prošek with Prosecco.hook: Tourist menus and gift shops — two unrelated wines, one name-collision
avoid:⚠ Confusing Prošek with Prosecco.text: Tourist menus and gift shops — two unrelated wines, one name-collision Croatian Prošek is a sweet straw-dried wine (cousin of Vin de Paille and Picolit) — nothing to do with Italian Prosecco , the dry sparkling Glera. Some shops and waiters exploit the confusion; some sell «Prošek» that is in fact thinned-down sweet plonk. Ask explicitly: «sweet, dessert wine» or «sparkling, dry». The legal dispute between Italy and Croatia over the protected name has been ongoing since 2021.

avoid:⚠ Pašticada served at peak summer.name: ⚠ Pašticada served at peak summer in tourist tavernas
avoid:⚠ Pašticada served at peak summer.hook: Riva and palace cards in July–August — a winter Sunday dish, microwaved to order
avoid:⚠ Pašticada served at peak summer.text: Riva and palace cards in July–August — a winter Sunday dish, microwaved to order Pašticada is a 24-hour vinegar marinade and a four-hour braise — a winter Sunday cathedral dish. In peak summer, almost no honest kitchen actually makes it from cold; what arrives at €25 in the palace cards is reheated stock from a sous-vide bag. Order it only at houses you can name: Apetit , Fife , an inland konoba — or wait until November.
